key_insight: MeanFlowNFT adapts forward-process RL from instantaneous-velocity diffusion models to MeanFlow’s average-velocity generators by learning an induced instantaneous predictor, enabling reward optimization without sacrificing few-step sampling speed.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical way to align fast generative models with human or task-specific rewards while keeping low sampling cost, which is important for deployable image and video generation systems.
method: Build an induced instantaneous-velocity predictor from MeanFlow’s average-velocity formulation.
Apply the DiffusionNFT forward-process RL objective to this predictor for well-defined reward optimization.
Keep sampling in the original average-velocity mode to preserve MeanFlow’s few-step efficiency.
evidence_signal: The method improves multiple benchmarks in image and video generation, outperforming prior RL-tuned few-step generators on 6 of 8 metrics for SD3.5-M and reaching a 4-step Wan 2.1 VBench score of 84.33 versus 82.57 for a 50-step RL baseline.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the induced velocity bridge, so implementation must preserve the MeanFlow identity and stable reward optimization across different sampling horizons.
paper_title: MeanFlowNFT: Bringing Forward-Process RL to Average-Velocity Generators
